content.text:
I fixed the "wholsale" → "wholesale" typo in every file that had it and committed the fix as a single commit, so `git revert HEAD` undoes all of it. `scripts/check.sh` passed before the commit.

**What changed:**
- **Committed:** one row each in `data/2025-10.csv`, `data/2025-11.csv` and `data/2025-12.csv`, all in the category column. There were no other occurrences anywhere in the repo.
- **Not committed:** `inbox/2025-12.csv` had the same typo, and I fixed it there too. But `inbox/` is gitignored, so that edit only exists on disk and a revert won't undo it. I fixed it anyway so that copying that file into `data/` again won't bring the typo back.

**Commit message:** this repo's messages start with a single month, but this fix covers three, so I used `2025-10..2025-12: fix category typo wholsale -> wholesale`. If your import log only understands one month per commit, tell me which prefix you want and I'll amend it. Nothing has been pushed.

A tool permission also blocked my first attempt (a `sed` command with a file glob), so I made the four edits one file at a time.
